case.question: How can I make picture-book time more interactive?

retrieved.text: Interactive picture-book time can include sounds, character actions and talking about the pictures with your toddler. Follow their interests rather than asking lots of questions.
retrieved.title: Make toddler picture-book reading interactive
retrieved.source_title: HSE: Sharing books with babies and young children

retrieved.text: Make picture-book reading a conversation: talk together about the pictures and how the objects shown are used.
retrieved.title: Interactive picture-book time at two years
retrieved.source_title: NHS: Chatting and building sentences, 2 to 3 years

retrieved.text: Look at picture with baby • Use any picture • Let child sit on your lap and look at the picture together • Point and name objects in the picture and describe what is happening in the picture • Ask child to name objects or parts of picture • Praise child when correct!
retrieved.title: Look at picture with baby

answer:
To make picture-book reading more interactive with your 24-month-old, try these simple steps:

* Add sounds and character actions during the story.
* Talk about the pictures together.
* Follow your toddler's interests rather than asking lots of questions.
